mainTopic: The end of the story of רבי יוסי and אליהו הנביא, the meaning of 'wicked people' in the משנה's teaching about עיר הנדחת, and a ברייתא about how the wicked and the righteous affect the world. This passage ends with the closing of מסכת סנהדרין.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a story. רבי יוסי had taught that אליהו was a קפדן (strict, quick to take offense). אליהו used to visit him, but then stayed away for three days. When he came back, רבי יוסי asked why, and אליהו answered, 'You called me קפדן!' רבי יוסי replied that this very reaction proves the point. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה's line, 'as long as there are רשעים in the world, there is anger in the world,' and asks who these רשעים are. רב יוסף answers: thieves. A ברייתא then teaches four cases, each backed by a פסוק: when a רשע comes, anger comes; when a רשע is gone, good comes; when a צדיק passes away, bad comes; and when a צדיק comes, good comes. The amud ends with the הדרן for פרק חלק and the completion of מסכת סנהדרין.

steps.title: אליהו stops visiting after being called strict
steps.stepSummary: The last word of רבי יוסי's teaching that אליהו was a קפדן, followed by אליהו staying away from רבי יוסי for three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אליהו] was strict. He used to come to [רבי יוסי]. He was hidden from him for three days and did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a story in the middle: רבי יוסי had taught that אליהו was a קפדן, and now אליהו, who normally visited him, stops coming for three days. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'קפדן הוה' finish רבי יוסי's statement on the previous amud. The point of the story is what happens next: אליהו's reaction to being called strict.

keyTerms.meaning: A strict, demanding, or short-tempered person
Used to, in the habit of
He was hidden, he did not show himself

phrases.english: was strict.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יוסי's teaching from right before here, that אליהו was strict.

phrases.english: He [Eliyahu] was used to coming to him [רבי יוסי].
He was hidden from him for three days,
and did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun on the previous amud, where רבי יוסי taught that אליהו was a קפדן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו, who visited רבי יוסי regularly, stayed away for three days after רבי יוסי called him strict.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks why אליהו stayed away
steps.stepSummary: When אליהו returns, רבי יוסי asks him why he did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came, he said to him: Why did the master not come?
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו finally comes back, and רבי יוסי asks him why he missed those three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי respectfully calls אליהו 'מר' (master). This question opens the way for אליהו to explain his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way to address someone

phrases.english: When he came, he said to him:
Why did the master not come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for the absence described in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אליהו stopped visiting for three days.

steps.title: אליהו complains about being called strict
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that he stayed away because רבי יוסי called him a קפדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You called me strict!
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו explains that he was hurt by being called a קפדן, and that is why he stayed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer works like a complaint against רבי יוסי's teaching. It sets up רבי יוסי's clever reply in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: You called me strict!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אליהו stayed away because he was offended at being called a קפדן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: your reaction proves my point
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that אליהו's staying away is itself proof that he is strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Here it is in front of us, that the master is being strict!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי turns the complaint around: by getting upset and staying away, אליהו is showing that he really is strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו's own behavior becomes the proof of the teaching. Instead of taking back his words, רבי יוסי shows that the reaction itself confirms them.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is, right in front of us
Is being strict, is taking offense

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי did not back down. אליהו's three-day absence over being called strict was itself proof that he was strict.

phrases.english: He said to him: Here it is in front of us,
that the master is being strict!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to אליהו's complaint in step 3 by using it as proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's teaching that אליהו was a קפדן
steps.raayaSupportSource: אליהו's own act of staying away for three days because he was offended

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the wicked bring anger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's teaching on the פסוק 'ולא ידבק בידך מאומה מן החרם': as long as there are רשעים in the world, there is anger in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And there shall not cling to your hand anything of the banned property.' As long as there are wicked people in the world, there is burning anger in the world, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to quote a line from the משנה. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about the property of an עיר הנדחת, which must be destroyed and not taken. The משנה learns from it a general rule: רשעים bring divine anger into the world. The word 'וכו׳' tells us the משנה continues beyond what is quoted here.

keyTerms.meaning: Banned property that may not be used, here the property of the עיר הנדחת

phrases.english: 'And there shall not cling to your hand
anything of the banned property' –
as long as there are wicked people in the world,
there is burning anger in the world, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה מִן הַחֵרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As long as there are רשעים in the world, there is divine anger in the world.

steps.title: Who are these wicked people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which רשעים the משנה is talking about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition: which wicked people bring anger into the world?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word 'רשעים' is very general. The גמרא wants to know exactly which type of sinner is meant.

phrases.english: Who are the wicked?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the רשעים in the משנה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: they are thieves
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the רשעים are thieves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the רשעים the משנה means are thieves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף narrows the general word 'רשעים' to one specific group: thieves. The גמרא does not explain his reason, but it fits the פסוק, which warns against taking banned property.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Thieves.

steps.title: ברייתא: the coming and passing of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a רשע comes into the world, anger comes, and when a רשע is gone, good comes. Each half is backed by a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When a wicked person comes into the world, anger comes into the world, as it says: 'When a wicked one comes, contempt also comes, and with shame, disgrace.' When a wicked person is gone from the world, good comes into the world, as it says: 'And when the wicked perish, there is joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that builds on the משנה's idea. It begins with the first two of four cases: a רשע coming and a רשע leaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (its rest is hidden behind 'וכו׳') said that רשעים bring anger and that when they are gone the anger leaves. The ברייתא goes further: when a רשע is gone, actual good enters the world. Each claim has its own פסוק.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: רָשָׁע בָּא לָעוֹלָם – חָרוֹן בָּא לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: When a wicked person comes into the world, anger comes into the world,
as it says: 'When a wicked one comes,
contempt also comes,
and with shame, disgrace.'
When a wicked person is gone from the world,
good comes into the world,
as it says: 'And when the wicked perish, there is joy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן רָשָׁע בָּא לָעוֹלָם חָרוֹן בָּא לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's idea from step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רשע's arrival brings anger to the world, and his removal brings good.

steps.title: ברייתא: the passing and coming of the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: when a צדיק leaves the world, bad comes, and when a צדיק comes into the world, good comes. The proofs are from ישעיהו and from the naming of נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When a righteous person leaves the world, bad comes into the world, as it says: 'The righteous one perishes and no one takes it to heart, and kind men are gathered in, with no one understanding that because of the coming evil the righteous one is gathered in.' When a righteous person comes into the world, good comes into the world, as it says: 'This one will comfort us for our work and for the pain of our hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its four cases with the צדיק: his passing brings hard times, and his arrival brings good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mirrors the רשע cases. The ישעיהו פסוק shows that a צדיק's death is connected to coming evil. The בראשית פסוק, said when נח was named, shows that a צדיק's birth brings comfort and blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: Four cases: a רשע coming brings anger, a רשע leaving brings good, a צדיק leaving brings bad, and a צדיק coming brings good.

phrases.aramaic: צַדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם – רָעָה בָּאָה לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: When a righteous person leaves the world, bad comes into the world,
as it says: 'The righteous one perishes
and no one takes it to heart,
and kind men are gathered in,
with no one understanding
that because of the coming evil the righteous one is gathered in.'

phrases.aramaic: צַדִּיק בָּא לָעוֹלָם – טוֹבָה בָּאָה לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: When a righteous person comes into the world, good comes into the world,
as it says: 'This one will comfort us
for our work and for the pain of our hands.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 5:29. This was said when נח was born and named.

steps.triggerLanguage: צַדִּיק נִפְטָר מִן הָעוֹלָם רָעָה בָּאָה לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 8, moving from רשעים to צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צדיק's passing brings bad to the world, and a צדיק's arrival brings good.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק חלק and מסכת סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק כל ישראל יש להם חלק, and the end of מסכת סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'All of Israel have a share,' and מסכת סנהדרין is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the discussion. It is the traditional closing line said when finishing a פרק, and here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' means 'we will return to you' and expresses the wish to come back and learn this פרק again. The extra words announce that מסכת סנהדרין is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing words of a פרק

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק
phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All of Israel have a share'
and Tractate Sanhedrin is complete

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק חלק and all of מסכת סנהדרין are complete.
